in_hebrew.name: פֶּנֶץ
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A name derived from the Hebrew word פֶּןֶן (pēnēn), meaning 'to buy, to purchase'. It can be interpreted as 'bought from God', 'purchased with God', or 'the one who is bought'. In the Bible, this name is found in the Old Testament, specifically in the Book of Joshua.

in_greek.name: Σπεντικός
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Σπεντικός (Spentikos) is derived from the Greek word σπένδομαι (spendōmai), meaning 'to spend, to pay'. It can be interpreted as 'expensive, costly, or 'the one who spends or pays'. In the Bible, this name is not explicitly found, but it may be implied in certain contexts, such as in the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15:11-32.

in_latin.name: Spentius
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Spentius is derived from the Latin word 'spendere', meaning 'to spend'. It can be interpreted as 'costly, expensive, or 'the one who spends'. In the Bible, this name is not explicitly found, but it may be implied in certain contexts, such as in the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25:14-30.
